title: Enosys AMM V3 (Flare + Songbird): $6.79M UniV3-fork TVL, $0 external-unprivileged extraction
categories_note: E-U $0: no external unprivileged path. H-O $6,793,213 is the DL nominal LP-owned TVL (on-chain Flare $6,728,825 + Songbird $62,238-$144,051), not attacker-extractable. P $0: no privileged-only bug; the 2/6 Safe can upgrade/drain the full TVL and a single EOA owns the Flare FTSO/monthly redistributors (~$8k WFLR), but these are centralization risks. S $0: no stuck principal (the unpriced dust pool holds 1 wei WFLR + 1,000 wei USDX; protocol fees $490 are collectible to ProfitDistribution).
live_targets_note: 168 pools (106 Flare + 62 Songbird) + 31 protocol/impl/admin contracts (2 factory proxies, 2 factory impls, 2 NPM proxies, 2 NPM impls, 2 pool impls, 4 history trackers, 2 reward managers, 2 epoch managers, 3 FTSO/monthly redistributors, 2 WNat registries, 2 Safes, 4 proxy admins, 2 ProfitDistribution receivers).
closed_reasons: Pool mint/swap/flash enforce post-callback balance checks; live eth_call from a non-paying caller reverts (M0/M1, IIA, F0/F1) at Flare block 72,386,500.
NPM decreaseLiquidity/collect/burn are isAuthorizedForToken; live collect and burn from a non-owner revert 'Not approved'; owner control succeeds.
Pool collectProtocol/setFeeProtocol/resetupDelegations are onlyFactoryOrFactoryOwner; live calls from an EOA revert 'NA'.
Factory owner/governor functions revert with the canonical owner/governor errors; owner and governor are the 2/6 Safe on both chains; no modules or guard.
History tracker writes require UPDATER/CLEANER roles; live updateLiquiditySnapshots from an EOA reverts 'HistoryStateTrackerBase: missing role'. UPDATER is held only by the NPM + every pool.
FTSO/Monthly claims are owner-gated; live non-owner claim reverts NotNftOwner(uint256) (0xb832bf93) and the owner control succeeds.
NPM, factory and ProfitDistribution hold 0 of all 16 pool tokens and 0 native; public sweepToken/unwrapWNat have nothing to take.
All 168 pools are consistent: factory() = factory, getPool = pool, feeAmountTickSpacing = tickSpacing, isPoolDeployedByFactory = true; no fake or unregistered pools.

Core Uniswap V3 math libraries are source-identical; the pool's custom code adds upgradeability, history snapshots and WNat delegation but preserves the canonical payment, position-key, lock and protocol-fee auth gates.

Top pool implied prices match DefiLlama/CoinGecko within rounding (stXRP/FXRP 0.9993 vs 0.996; CDP/USDT0 0.994 vs 0.993; WFLR/FXRP 0.00503 vs 0.00502; FXRP/USDT0 1.293 vs 1.292; sFLR/WFLR 1.882 vs 1.894); no stale-price/arb gap in material pools.

poc.note: Nine negative-control Foundry tests (mint/swap/flash no-pay, NPM collect/burn non-owner, pool collectProtocol/setFeeProtocol, factory admin, fixed-recipient collectProtocolFees, live pool state) were written and forge build succeeds. They were not run locally per the campaign instruction; the parent CI should run poc/run.sh and fill tests_passed/ci_run_urls.

caveats: The current Flare pool implementation 0x23f02a... and factory implementation 0xd835... are unverified. The verified predecessor 0xC07b... is the same family (24,204 B) but differs in one internal snapshot region; the current pool is opcode-identical to Songbird 0xfcba... and the current NPM source is verified on Songbird 0xb126... . The negative verdict rests on live behavior plus the verified family; a hidden fund-moving path in the unverified current bytecode cannot be excluded without its source.
Songbird TVL is price-source sensitive: DefiLlama $62,238 vs local DEX mark $144,051 (USDX at $1, SFIN ~$98, FXRP $1.30). Songbird is 0.9-2.1% of total; the verdict is unchanged.
The FTSO/monthly redistributors and one history tracker implementation are unverified; only their public claim/setter auth and balances were tested.
The 2/6 Safe is below the documented 4/6. Any two signers can upgrade every pool and move the full ~$6.79M. This is a privileged centralization risk, not an E-U path.
The Flare FTSO/monthly redistributors are owned by a single EOA (0x51578d...); ~$8k of WFLR plus delegation/claim setup is exposed to that key.

createPool is permissionless and can bloat the pools array; the unpriced dust pool can be initialized to make collectProtocolFeesAll() revert. Ranged collectProtocolFees(start,count) still works. Griefing only, no value extraction.
No Foundry tests were run locally per the campaign instruction; the parent CI should run poc/run.sh and update tests_passed/ci_run_urls.
No keyed RPC URLs or secrets were written; all RPCs in the evidence are public keyless endpoints.
one_liner: Enosys AMM V3 holds ~$6.79M across 168 UniV3-fork pools on Flare/Songbird; the fork keeps canonical payment, position-auth, protocol-fee and role gates (all live-tested), and no external unprivileged value-extraction path was found ($0 E-U, high confidence); residual risk is the 2/6 upgrade Safe, a single-EOA FTSO owner, and unverified current pool/factory implementations.
